verses.text: The wicked flee when no man pursues (chases). But the righteous (people right with God) are bold as a lion.
For the transgression (sin) of a land, its princes are many. But by a man of understanding and knowledge, its state will be prolonged (lengthened).
A poor man who oppresses (crushes) the poor is like a sweeping rain. It leaves no food.
Those who forsake (leave) the law praise the wicked. But those who keep the law contend (fight) with them.
Evil men do not understand judgment (what is right). But those who seek the LORD understand all things.
Better is the poor man who walks in his uprightness (honesty). He is better than one perverse (crooked) in his ways, though he is rich.
Whoever keeps the law is a wise son. But the one who is a companion of riotous (wild) men shames his father.
One may increase his substance (wealth) by usury (interest) and unjust gain. He will gather it for the one who will pity the poor.
One may turn away his ear from hearing the law. Even his prayer will be an abomination (something hated).
Someone may cause the righteous (people right with God) to go astray in an evil way. He will fall himself into his own pit. But the upright (honest people) will have good things in possession.
The rich man is wise in his own conceit (proud imagination). But the poor man who has understanding searches him out.
When righteous (right with God) men rejoice, there is great glory. But when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.
The one who covers his sins will not prosper. But whoever confesses and forsakes (leaves) them will have mercy.
Happy is the man who fears always. But the one who hardens his heart will fall into mischief (harm).
Like a roaring lion, and a ranging (roaming) bear. So is a wicked ruler over the poor people.
The prince who wants (lacks) understanding is also a great oppressor (one who crushes others). But the one who hates covetousness (wanting what belongs to others) will prolong (lengthen) his days.
A man who does violence to any person's blood will flee to the pit. Let no man stay (stop) him.
Whoever walks uprightly (honestly) will be saved. But the one who is perverse (crooked) in his ways will fall at once.
The one who tills (works) his land will have plenty of bread. But the one who follows after vain (worthless) persons will have poverty enough.
A faithful man will abound (overflow) with blessings. But the one who makes haste (hurries) to be rich will not be innocent.
To have respect of persons (show favor to some) is not good. For a piece of bread that man will transgress (sin).
The one who hastes (hurries) to be rich has an evil eye (jealousy). He does not consider that poverty will come upon him.
One who rebukes (scolds) a man will afterwards find more favor. He finds more than the one who flatters with the tongue.
Whoever robs his father or his mother, and says: It is no transgression (sin). The same is the companion of a destroyer.
The one who is of a proud heart stirs up strife (fighting). But whoever puts his trust in the LORD will be made fat (rich).
The one who trusts in his own heart is a fool. But whoever walks wisely will be delivered (rescued).
The one who gives to the poor will not lack. But the one who hides his eyes will have many a curse.
When the wicked rise, men hide themselves. But when the wicked perish (are destroyed), the righteous (people right with God) increase.

verses.text: A man may be often reproved (corrected), yet harden his neck. He will suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy (cure).
When the righteous (people right with God) are in authority, the people rejoice. But when the wicked bear rule (rule), the people mourn.
Whoever loves wisdom rejoices (makes glad) his father. But the one who keeps company with harlots (prostitutes) spends his substance (wealth).
The king by judgment (what is right) establishes (makes firm) the land. But the one who receives gifts (bribes) overthrows it.
A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
In the transgression (sin) of an evil man there is a snare (trap). But the righteous (right with God) man sings and rejoices.
The righteous (right with God) man considers the cause (case) of the poor. But the wicked does not regard (care) to know it.
Scornful (mocking) men bring a city into a snare (trap). But wise men turn away wrath (anger).
A wise man may contend (argue) with a foolish man. If so, whether he rages or laughs, there is no rest.
The bloodthirsty hate the upright (honest person). But the just (those who are right with God) seek his soul.
A fool utters (speaks out) all his mind. But a wise man keeps it in until afterwards.
If a ruler hearkens (listens) to lies, all his servants are wicked.
The poor and the deceitful (lying) man meet together. The LORD lightens (gives light to) both their eyes.
The king who faithfully judges the poor, his throne will be established (made firm) forever.
The rod and reproof (correction) give wisdom. But a child left to himself brings his mother to shame.
When the wicked are multiplied, transgression (sin) increases. But the righteous (people right with God) will see their fall.
Correct your son, and he will give you rest. Yes, he will give delight to your soul.
Where there is no vision, the people perish (are destroyed). But the one who keeps the law, happy is he.
A servant will not be corrected by words. For though he understands, he will not answer.
Do you see a man who is hasty (quick) in his words? There is more hope of a fool than of him.
One may delicately (gently) bring up his servant from a child. At the length (in the end) the servant will become his son.
An angry man stirs up strife (fighting). And a furious man abounds (overflows) in transgression (sin).
A man's pride will bring him low. But honor will uphold (hold up) the humble in spirit.
Whoever is partner with a thief hates his own soul. He hears cursing, but does not bewray (give away) it.
The fear of man brings a snare (trap). But whoever puts his trust in the LORD will be safe.
Many seek the ruler's favor. But every man's judgment comes from the LORD.
An unjust man is an abomination (something hated) to the just (those who are right with God). And whoever is upright (honest) in the way is an abomination (something hated) to the wicked.

verses.text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy (message). The man spoke to Ithiel, even to Ithiel and Ucal.
Surely I am more brutish (stupid like an animal) than any man. I do not have the understanding of a man.
I have not learned wisdom. I do not have the knowledge of the holy.

Who has ascended (gone up) into heaven, or descended (come down)? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has bound the waters in a garment? Who has established (set in place) all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is His Son's name, if you can tell?
Every word of God is pure. He is a shield to those who put their trust in Him.
Do not add to His words. Otherwise He will reprove (correct) you, and you will be found a liar.
Two things I have required (asked) of You. Do not deny (refuse) them to me before I die.
Remove vanity (emptiness) and lies far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with food convenient (right) for me.
Otherwise I may be full, and deny You, and say: Who is the LORD? Or I may be poor, and steal. Then I would take the name of my God in vain (dishonor it).
Do not accuse a servant to his master. Otherwise the servant will curse you, and you will be found guilty.
There is a generation (group of people) that curses their father. They do not bless their mother.
There is a generation (group of people) that is pure in their own eyes. Yet they are not washed from their filthiness.
There is a generation (group of people), O how lofty (proud) are their eyes! Their eyelids are lifted up.
There is a generation (group of people) whose teeth are like swords. Their jaw teeth are like knives. They devour (eat up) the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.
The horseleach (bloodsucking worm) has two daughters, crying: Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied. Yes, four things do not say: It is enough.
The grave, and the barren (childless) womb. The earth that is not filled with water. And the fire that does not say: It is enough.
The eye that mocks at his father, and despises (looks down on) obeying his mother. The ravens of the valley will pick it out. The young eagles will eat it.
There are three things that are too wonderful for me. Yes, four that I do not know:
The way of an eagle in the air. The way of a serpent (snake) on a rock. The way of a ship in the middle of the sea. And the way of a man with a maid (young woman).
Such is the way of an adulterous (unfaithful in marriage) woman. She eats, and wipes her mouth, and says: I have done no wickedness.
For three things the earth is disquieted (troubled). For four it cannot bear:
For a servant when he reigns (rules). And a fool when he is filled with meat (food).
For an odious (hated) woman when she is married. And a handmaid (servant girl) who is heir to her mistress.
There are four things that are little on the earth. But they are exceeding (very) wise:
The ants are a people not strong. Yet they prepare their meat (food) in the summer.
The conies (rock badgers) are only a feeble (weak) folk (people). Yet they make their houses in the rocks.
The locusts (grasshoppers) have no king. Yet they all go forth by bands (in groups).
The spider takes hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces.
There are three things that go well. Yes, four are comely (beautiful) in going:
A lion, which is strongest among beasts (animals). It does not turn away for any.
A greyhound (swift dog), and a he goat also. And a king, against whom there is no rising up.
You may have done foolishly in lifting up yourself. Or you may have thought evil. If so, lay your hand on your mouth.
Surely the churning of milk brings forth butter. The wringing of the nose brings forth blood. So the forcing of wrath (anger) brings forth strife (fighting).

verses.text: Better is the poor man who walks in his integrity (honesty). He is better than one perverse (crooked) in his lips who is a fool.
Also, for the soul to be without knowledge is not good. And the one who hastes (hurries) with his feet sins.
The foolishness of man perverts (twists) his way. And his heart frets (is angry) against the LORD.
Wealth makes many friends. But the poor man is separated from his neighbor.
A false witness will not be unpunished. The one who speaks lies will not escape.
Many will intreat (beg for) the favor of the prince. Every man is a friend to the one who gives gifts.
All the brethren (brothers) of the poor man hate him. How much more do his friends go far from him? He pursues (chases) them with words, yet they are wanting (gone).
The one who gets wisdom loves his own soul. The one who keeps understanding will find good.
A false witness will not be unpunished. The one who speaks lies will perish (be destroyed).
Delight is not seemly (fitting) for a fool. Much less is it fitting for a servant to rule over princes.
The discretion (careful thinking) of a man defers (holds back) his anger. It is his glory to pass over a transgression (sin).
The king's wrath (anger) is like the roaring of a lion. But his favor is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is the calamity (disaster) of his father. The contentions (fights) of a wife are a continual dropping (dripping).
House and riches are the inheritance of fathers. But a prudent (sensible) wife is from the LORD.
Slothfulness (laziness) casts into a deep sleep. An idle (doing nothing) soul will suffer hunger.
The one who keeps the commandment keeps his own soul. But the one who despises (looks down on) his ways will die.
The one who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD. The LORD will pay him back what he has given.
Chasten (correct) your son while there is hope. Do not let your soul spare for his crying.
A man of great wrath (anger) will suffer punishment. For if you deliver (rescue) him, you must do it again.
Hear counsel (advice), and receive instruction (correction). Then you may be wise in your latter end.
There are many devices (plans) in a man's heart. Nevertheless (but) the counsel (advice) of the LORD, that will stand.
The desire of a man is his kindness. And a poor man is better than a liar.
The fear of the LORD (deep respect for the LORD) leads to life. The one who has it will abide (stay) satisfied. He will not be visited with evil.
A slothful (lazy) man hides his hand in his bosom (chest). He will not even bring it to his mouth again.
Smite (hit) a scorner (mocker), and the simple (people easily fooled) will beware. Reprove (correct) one who has understanding, and he will understand knowledge.
A son may waste (rob) his father and chase away his mother. That son causes shame and brings reproach (shame).
Cease (stop), my son, to hear the instruction (correction) that causes you to err (go wrong). It leads you away from the words of knowledge.
An ungodly witness scorns (mocks) judgment (what is right). The mouth of the wicked devours (eats up) iniquity (sin).
Judgments are prepared for scorners (mockers), and stripes (lashes) for the back of fools.

verses.text: Wine is a mocker. Strong drink is raging. Whoever is deceived (fooled) by it is not wise.
The fear of a king is like the roaring of a lion. Whoever provokes (stirs) him to anger sins against his own soul.
It is an honor for a man to cease (stop) from strife (fighting). But every fool will be meddling.
The sluggard (lazy person) will not plow because of the cold. So he will beg in harvest, and have nothing.
Counsel (advice) in the heart of man is like deep water. But a man of understanding will draw it out.
Most men will proclaim (announce) each one his own goodness. But who can find a faithful man?
The just (right with God) man walks in his integrity (honesty). His children are blessed after him.
A king sits on the throne of judgment. He scatters away all evil with his eyes.
Who can say: I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
Divers (different) weights and divers (different) measures are both an abomination (something hated) to the LORD.
Even a child is known by his doings. It shows whether his work is pure, and whether it is right.
The hearing ear and the seeing eye, the LORD has made both of them.
Do not love sleep, or you will come to poverty. Open your eyes, and you will be satisfied with bread.
It is naught (worthless), it is naught (worthless), says the buyer. But when he has gone his way, then he boasts (brags).
There is gold, and a multitude of rubies. But the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
Take the garment of one who is surety (promise to pay the debt) for a stranger. Take a pledge (something held as a promise) from him for a strange woman (a woman who is not your wife).
Bread of deceit (lying) is sweet to a man. But afterwards his mouth will be filled with gravel.
Every purpose (plan) is established (made firm) by counsel (advice). With good advice make war.
The one who goes about as a talebearer (gossip) reveals secrets. So do not meddle with the one who flatters with his lips.
A man may curse his father or his mother. His lamp will be put out in obscure (deep) darkness.
An inheritance may be gotten hastily (quickly) at the beginning. But its end will not be blessed.
Do not say: I will recompense (repay) evil. But wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
Divers (different) weights are an abomination (something hated) to the LORD. A false balance (dishonest scale) is not good.
Man's goings (steps) are of the LORD. How then can a man understand his own way?
It is a snare (trap) to the man who devours (eats up) what is holy. It is a snare to make enquiry (ask questions) after vows (promises to God).
A wise king scatters the wicked. He brings the wheel (threshing wheel) over them.
The spirit of man is the candle (lamp) of the LORD. It searches all the inward parts of the belly (stomach).
Mercy and truth preserve (protect) the king. His throne is upholden (held up) by mercy.
The glory of young men is their strength. The beauty of old men is the gray head.
The blueness (bruising) of a wound cleanses away evil. So do stripes (lashes) the inward parts of the belly (stomach).

verses.text: The words of King Lemuel, the prophecy (message) that his mother taught him.
What, my son? And what, the son of my womb? And what, the son of my vows (promises to God)?
Do not give your strength to women. Do not give your ways to that which destroys kings.
It is not for kings, O Lemuel. It is not for kings to drink wine. It is not for princes to drink strong drink.
Otherwise they may drink, and forget the law. They may pervert (twist) the judgment (what is right) of any of the afflicted (suffering).
Give strong drink to the one who is ready to perish (be destroyed). Give wine to those who have heavy (sad) hearts.
Let him drink, and forget his poverty. Let him remember his misery no more.
Open your mouth for the dumb (those who cannot speak). Speak in the cause (case) of all who are appointed to destruction.
Open your mouth, and judge righteously (rightly). Plead the cause (case) of the poor and needy.
Who can find a virtuous (good and strong) woman? For her price is far above rubies.
The heart of her husband safely trusts in her. So her husband will have no need of spoil (stolen goods).
She will do her husband good and not evil. She will do so all her life.
She seeks wool and flax (plant used for linen). She works willingly with her hands.
She is like the merchants' ships. She brings her food from far away.
She rises also while it is yet night. She gives meat (food) to her household (family), and a portion (share) to her maidens (young women servants).
She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard (grape farm).
She girds (wraps) her loins (waist) with strength. She strengthens her arms.
She perceives (understands) that her merchandise (trade) is good. Her candle (lamp) does not go out by night.
She lays her hands to the spindle (spinning stick). Her hands hold the distaff (stick that holds the wool).
She stretches out her hand to the poor. Yes, she reaches forth her hands to the needy.
She is not afraid of the snow for her household (family). For all her household (family) are clothed with scarlet (bright red).
She makes herself coverings of tapestry (rich cloth). Her clothing is silk and purple.
Her husband is known in the gates. He sits among the elders of the land.
She makes fine linen, and sells it. She delivers (hands over) girdles (belts) to the merchant.
Strength and honor are her clothing. And she will rejoice in time to come.
She opens her mouth with wisdom. In her tongue is the law of kindness.
She looks well to the ways of her household (family). She does not eat the bread of idleness (doing nothing).
Her children arise up, and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her.
Many daughters have done virtuously (well). But you excel (do better than) them all.
Favor is deceitful (lying), and beauty is vain (empty). But a woman who fears the LORD (deeply respects the LORD), she will be praised.
Give her of the fruit of her hands. Let her own works praise her in the gates.
